name: Report borrowing base and covenants to banks
summary: New leases are first funded on a syndicated bank credit line, and the banks lend only against eligible receivables and only while the company meets its financial covenants. Each month the treasury analyst extracts the receivables on the line, applies the eligibility rules and concentration caps, calculates availability, reconciles it to the books and, after treasurer review, has the CFO sign the borrowing base certificate. After the month-end close the analyst also calculates the financial and portfolio covenants, the controller confirms the figures, the treasurer reviews headroom and the CFO signs the compliance certificate, with a waiver request when a covenant is breached. Waiting for the close, spreadsheet definitions that differ from accounting and late data make it slow and error-prone.

baseline.org_archetype: A privately owned Canadian independent equipment lessor that warehouses new contracts on a syndicated revolving credit facility before selling them to conduits.
baseline.notes: One borrowing base certificate and one compliance certificate a month; quarter-end certificates add interest coverage and commentary. Annual lender field examinations are outside this case.

unit_of_work: one borrowing base or compliance report
trigger: Month-end portfolio data are loaded (borrowing base) or the month's financial statements are released (compliance certificate).
end_state: The signed borrowing base certificate or compliance certificate is delivered to the agent bank and any questions are answered.

volume.seasonality: Quarter-end certificates take longer; 2020 brought deferral-related questions and waiver talks.

evidence.note: Organisation file range; monthly borrowing base and compliance certificate as in the sample clauses. Revolving bank syndicates are documented at Canadian equipment lessors.
Loaded cost from the organisation file (2019-2022 wage times 1.35). Two reports a month plus lender questions and the annual field examination.
Loaded cost from the organisation file (2019-2022 wage times 1.35). Reviews both reports and handles overadvances and lender contact.

systems.name: Data warehouse and business intelligence reports
Lease management system (contracts, schedules, billing, tax codes, asset records, servicing)
Spreadsheet models (pool cuts, borrowing base, covenants, budget, tax workpapers)
General ledger and accounts payable (mid-market ERP)
Bank cash management portal for pre-authorised debit files, EFT payments and wires
Document imaging and contract file store

steps.name: Open the month's lender reporting checklist
steps.description: After month-end the treasury and cash analyst opens the reporting calendar, confirms which reports the credit agreement requires this month (the monthly borrowing base and the monthly or quarter-end compliance certificate), copies last month's workbooks and starts the report that is due first.

error.defect_description: Wrong template or prior-month workbook used.

evidence.note: Monthly borrowing base and compliance reporting follow the sample clauses; the one-each split follows the organisation file's two reports a month.

steps.name: Extract the receivables on the bank line
steps.description: The analyst runs the warehouse report of contracts funded on the bank warehouse line and not yet sold to a conduit, with net investment, days past due, obligor, vendor, equipment type, province, booking date, term and any modification, and pastes it into the borrowing base workbook.

error.defect_description: Contracts sold to a conduit in the month left in the listing.

evidence.note: The wait reflects daily cash work and month-end pool sales that come first; an author estimate.

steps.name: Apply the eligibility criteria and calculate ineligibles
steps.description: The analyst applies the credit agreement's eligibility rules in the workbook: excludes contracts past due beyond the limit, defaulted, restructured or deferred, with insolvent or foreign obligors, without a perfected registration or on the line too long, and cuts amounts above obligor, vendor and used-equipment concentration caps.

error.defect_description: A concentration cap or delinquency cut-off applied wrongly.

control.basis: Credit agreement: definition of eligible receivables and concentration limits

evidence.note: Exclusions follow sample definitions; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Calculate availability under the facility
steps.description: The analyst multiplies eligible receivables by the advance rate, deducts the reserves the agreement sets, compares the result with loans and letters of credit outstanding from the bank statement and shows the excess availability or an overadvance.

error.defect_description: Loan balance taken from the wrong date.

evidence.note: Advance-rate mechanics are standard; the overadvance rate is an author estimate (pool sales keep the line within its limit).

steps.name: Resolve an overadvance
steps.description: The treasurer decides how to bring loans back under the borrowing base, usually by repaying from cash or bringing forward a pool sale, calls the agent bank and records the agreed cure.

control.basis: Credit agreement: mandatory prepayment when loans exceed the borrowing base

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Reconcile the borrowing base to the ledger and the bank
steps.description: The analyst ties the total receivables in the listing to the lease subledger and general ledger, less contracts sold to conduits, and the loan balance to the agent bank's statement, and explains differences.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: lender reports agree to the books

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Treasurer reviews the borrowing base
steps.description: The treasurer checks the movement in eligibles and ineligibles against last month, the concentration cuts and the availability, and approves the report or returns it.

control.basis: Treasury procedure: preparer and reviewer of lender reports differ

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: CFO signs the borrowing base certificate
steps.description: The chief financial officer reads the summary and signs the certificate that the borrowing base is accurate and complete and that no default has occurred.

control.basis: Credit agreement: certificate signed by a responsible or financial officer

evidence.note: Sample clauses name the CFO or controller as certifying officer.

steps.name: Submit the borrowing base to the agent bank
steps.description: The analyst uploads the signed certificate with the receivables listing, aging and ineligibles schedule to the agent bank's portal or sends it by secure email, and files a copy.

control.basis: Credit agreement: monthly delivery deadline for the borrowing base

evidence.note: Delivery within 10 to 30 days of month-end in sample clauses.

steps.name: Agent bank reviews the borrowing base
steps.description: The agent's credit team checks the certificate against prior months and its own collateral monitoring and may ask about large ineligibles, concentrations or delinquency changes.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Answer the agent's questions
steps.description: The analyst sends contract detail and explanations for the items queried and, if an error is found, a corrected certificate for signature.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Collect the closed financial statements and the risk report
steps.description: For the compliance certificate the analyst waits for accounting to release the month's financial statements and for risk to issue the monthly portfolio report, then pulls the trial balance, debt balances and delinquency and loss figures.

error.defect_description: Draft rather than final statements used.

evidence.note: The close takes about 11 calendar days in efc-close-the-month and the risk report is presented about 15 days after month-end (efc-monitor-portfolio-risk); treasury gets its extract before the committee.

steps.name: Calculate the financial covenants
steps.description: The analyst calculates the ratios exactly as the credit agreement defines them: total debt to tangible net worth, minimum tangible net worth and, at quarter-ends, interest coverage on trailing earnings, with the agreed adjustments for securitisation debt and subordinated debt.

error.defect_description: A definition applied wrongly, for example securitisation debt counted in leverage.

evidence.note: Ratio types follow the sources; the leverage and net worth covenants typical of finance companies are author estimates.

steps.name: Calculate the portfolio covenants
steps.description: From the risk report and warehouse data the analyst calculates the portfolio tests, such as receivables more than 60 days past due and annualised net charge-offs as a share of the portfolio, and the share of deferred contracts in 2020, and compares them with the limits.

evidence.note: Portfolio performance covenants are common in lessor facilities; specific tests are author estimates.

steps.name: Controller confirms the figures and adjustments
steps.description: The controller checks that the ledger figures, debt totals and covenant adjustments match the released statements and accounting policies, especially lease accounting and loss allowance effects, and signs the workbook or returns it.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: accounting review of figures sent to lenders

evidence.note: Lenders expect supporting workpapers for each certificate input.

steps.name: Treasurer reviews covenant headroom
steps.description: The treasurer compares each result with its limit and with the forecast for the next quarters and decides whether the company is in compliance or needs to ask the lenders for a waiver or amendment.

evidence.note: Breach frequency is an author estimate; it was higher in 2020.

steps.name: Request a waiver or amendment from the syndicate
steps.description: The chief financial officer calls the agent bank, explains the cause and the plan, and sends a written request for a waiver or a covenant amendment, often with a fee and tighter reporting.

control.basis: Credit agreement: covenant waivers need the consent of the required lenders

evidence.note: Early conversations with lenders are recommended; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Syndicate lenders consider the waiver
steps.description: The agent circulates the request, each lender's credit team reviews it and the required lenders consent, sometimes after negotiating the fee or conditions.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Record the waiver terms
steps.description: The analyst updates the covenant workbook and the reporting calendar with the waiver or amended levels, any new reporting and the fee, and notes it on the certificate.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the compliance certificate
steps.description: The analyst fills the certificate form attached to the credit agreement with each covenant calculation and limit, confirms that no default exists, and attaches the financial statements and, at quarter-ends, the required commentary.

error.defect_description: Figures transcribed wrongly onto the form.

evidence.note: Times are author estimates.

steps.name: CFO signs the compliance certificate
steps.description: The chief financial officer reviews the certificate and supporting schedule and signs it as the responsible officer certifying the calculations and that no default has occurred.

control.basis: Credit agreement: compliance certificate signed by a responsible officer; a false certificate is an event of default

evidence.note: The organisation file says the CFO signs the certificate.

steps.name: Deliver the certificate to the agent bank
steps.description: The analyst sends the signed certificate and statements to the agent bank for the syndicate before the deadline, because a late certificate can raise pricing or become a default, and files a copy.

control.basis: Credit agreement: reporting deadlines (late certificates trigger the highest pricing level in the sample agreement)

exceptions.name: Overadvance
exceptions.description: Loans exceed the borrowing base and the treasurer arranges a repayment or an earlier pool sale.

exceptions.name: Borrowing base does not tie
exceptions.description: The listing does not agree to the ledger or the bank and is corrected.

exceptions.name: Agent questions
exceptions.description: The agent bank queries ineligibles, concentrations or delinquency.

exceptions.name: Covenant figures corrected
exceptions.description: The controller finds a figure or definition error and the covenants are recalculated.

exceptions.name: Covenant breach and waiver
exceptions.description: A covenant is breached or about to be and the CFO obtains a waiver or amendment before the certificate goes out.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from month-end to delivery of the report
benchmarks.population: Canadian independent equipment lessor with a syndicated warehouse facility, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author estimate within the sample deadlines: borrowing base 10 to 30 days after month-end, monthly statements 20 to 30 days, quarterly certificates 45 days.

pain_points.description: Eligibility rules and concentration caps live in a spreadsheet and are applied by hand each month, so errors appear when the bank or the reviewer checks them.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

pain_points.description: The compliance certificate cannot start until accounting releases the statements and risk issues its report, which leaves little time before the deadline.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

pain_points.description: Covenant definitions differ from accounting figures (securitisation debt, subordinated debt, lease accounting), which causes rework between treasury and the controller.

evidence.note: Adjustments may need lender consent and supporting workpapers.

pain_points.description: A projected breach needs weeks of syndicate approval for a waiver.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

sources.title: Borrowing base certificate (sample clauses from credit agreements)
sources.supports: Sample clauses require an updated borrowing base certificate within 10, 15 or 30 days after each month-end, certified by a responsible officer or by the chief financial officer or corporate controller, delivered with the borrowing base reports, and more often after certain events.

sources.title: Eligible lease receivables (definitions from credit agreements)
sources.supports: Sample definitions exclude leases more than 61 days (or 120 days) past due, in default, not subject to a first priority perfected security interest, restructured for credit reasons, with foreign lessees, older than 210 days or above lessee and used-equipment concentration caps.

sources.title: Monthly financial statements; compliance certificates (sample clauses)
sources.supports: Monthly statements due 20 or 30 days after month-end; a quarterly compliance certificate due 45 days after quarter-end and an annual one 120 days after year-end, signed by a responsible officer.

sources.title: Debt covenant deadlines are coming: how private companies prepare for the audit
sources.supports: Compliance certificates are signed officer certifications of the ratio calculations, filed each quarter and at year-end, commonly due 30, 45 or 60 days after period close; typical ratios are leverage, interest coverage and fixed charge coverage; lenders expect supporting workpapers and early conversations about adjustments.

sources.title: Credit agreement dated December 15, 2005 (exhibit 10.12), Canadian dollar revolving tranche
sources.supports: A syndicated revolving credit agreement with a Canadian dollar tranche agented by a Canadian bank; pricing is set by the leverage ratio in the latest compliance certificate and the highest pricing level applies if a certificate is late.

sources.title: Chesswood announces fiscal year 2021 results
sources.supports: A Canadian equipment finance group formed a new revolver syndicate in 2021 and reports non-GAAP measures based on the requirements of its significant banking and lending agreements.

sources.title: Financial/Securitization Analyst (job posting)
sources.supports: A Toronto non-bank lender with equipment leasing: produces monthly compliance reports, makes borrowing requests, sends regular reports to funders and supports funder audits; Excel and Great Plains.

assumptions: One borrowing base certificate and one compliance certificate a month make the two cases; quarter-end certificates are covered by the high ends of the time ranges.
The risk report trigger arrives inside the compliance case (step s12), so it has a share of zero.
The borrowing base also goes to daily cash management, which lists it as an input (efc-manage-daily-cash); the organisation file's process map does not list that link.
Advance rates, eligibility rules, covenant types and limits are private; those described are typical of lessor warehouse facilities and sample clauses, not the company's actual terms.
The CFO signs both certificates; some agreements accept the controller or treasurer as responsible officer.
Annual field examinations and audits of the borrowing base by the agent bank are outside this case but add to the analyst's time on the process.
External steps have no touch time; lender reviews and waiver consents are in wait_before_min.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (2019-2022 wage times 1.35).
